_comment: F4 shape — docs/E2E.md section 2 'F4 - shape-matched synthetic corpora' and section 0
(the seven corrections table, C1-C7). Every number below is either copied verbatim from a
committed document, or marked 'derived' with the arithmetic that produces it from numbers
that are. None of it is read from seed/ (Zone 1 law, wealthy/CLAUDE.md; this repo's own
docs/BRIEF.md rule 9) - gen_corpus.py must never open the real export.
This mirrors census.raw (the 567-row RAW export), not census.authored (the 308-row subset)
- 'shape.json mirrors census.raw, so F4 is a stand-in for the export, not for the import'
(docs/E2E.md section 2). Two fields below are explicitly authored-subset numbers used as a
documented modeling choice (see vertical_weight_source and completion_by_vertical), because
the raw export's own per-vertical split is never published anywhere - only the authored
one is. Applying it to the whole synthetic N is a stated approximation, not a measured fact.
ARCHITECTURE.md section 0's own completion table is STALE on one number and docs/E2E.md's
C3 correction supersedes it: day is 127 authored rows with 125 done (98%), not 126/125/99%,
and the 'none' bucket is 88, not 89. Values below use the corrected (E2E.md) figures.
Every nested object below (depth_histogram, fanout, ...) is pure data, consumed by key —
none of them carries its own _comment. Provenance for each lives in the sibling
_comment_<field> key at this top level instead, so gen_corpus.py never has to filter a
documentation key out of a dict it iterates as weights or counts.
source: ARCHITECTURE.md section 0 (published aggregate), corrected by docs/E2E.md section 0 C3/C4/C7
_comment_depth_histogram: docs/E2E.md section 2 F4 paragraph, verbatim. Sums to 567 (raw). Scales exactly for N in {567, 5670, 56700} since both are integer multiples of 567.
_comment_fanout: docs/E2E.md section 0: 'Parents: 50 over the raw export, 49 over the authored subset.' mean/median/max from ARCHITECTURE.md section 0. gen_corpus.py respects max as a hard cap; mean/median are targets, not exact reproductions (see module docstring).
_comment_field_usage_pct_raw: ARCHITECTURE.md section 0's field-usage table, over all 567 raw rows.
_comment_title: ARCHITECTURE.md section 0 / docs/E2E.md section 2 F4 paragraph, verbatim.
_comment_body: docs/E2E.md section 2 F4 paragraph and D9 (line 2460): '35 bodies at median 218 chars and a longest body of 3453 chars.' present_count is raw-scale (35 of 567); scales exactly at 5670/56700.
_comment_cross_vertical_parent_child: ARCHITECTURE.md section 0, 'Cross-vertical' line. Not individually reproduced by the generator (no per-pair placement logic) - recorded for completeness and because the deepest real chain (life -> decade -> year -> quarter -> quarter -> day -> unscheduled) motivated the depth-6 bucket above.
_comment_densest_column_raw: docs/E2E.md section 4 limits table, 'ids in a bulk PATCH' row: 'the densest single column in the export holds 14 rows, ~140 at F4-5670.' gen_corpus.py forces exactly round(14 * N / 567) rows into one shared (vertical=month, fixed period) column so AC-190's no-cap assertion (ridden by S-92) has a real dense column to count against.
_comment_search_plant: docs/E2E.md S-94 / AC-094: 'the generator plants 40 known matches and all 40 return.' Fixed count, NOT scaled by N - S-94 only runs at F4-5670, and 40 is the literal number both documents state.
_comment_vertical_weight_source: docs/E2E.md section 0 C3 (corrected): the AUTHORED 308-row per-vertical breakdown, day 127 (not ARCHITECTURE.md's stale 126), none bucket 88 (not 89). Applied to the FULL synthetic N as gen_corpus.py's vertical-assignment weights - a documented modeling choice: raw's own per-vertical split is never published (it is dominated by the 247 calendar + 12 onboarding rows this generator does not simulate), so the authored proportions are the best available anchor, not a measured raw-scale fact.
_comment_completion_by_vertical: ARCHITECTURE.md section 0, corrected by docs/E2E.md C3 (day: 125/127 = 98%, not 125/126 = 99%). Fraction of rows assigned that vertical which gen_corpus.py marks done.
_comment_created_at_burst: ARCHITECTURE.md section 0's abandonment histogram - 'every one of the 567 goals was created in a 4-month burst', ASCII chart. Sums to 567; scales exactly at 5670/56700. 2024-12-16 is excluded from day-of-month sampling within this month (30 other days remain) so no generated created_datetime can literally collide with tools/import_planner.py's CALENDAR_BATCH_CREATED_AT sentinel (2024-12-16T17:29:22+03:00), which would misclassify a synthetic export row as calendar_timed/calendar_allday.
